Converted intersection to all-way stop control (AWSC):
- Installed dual-indicated Stop signs (R1-1) with All Way plaques (R1-3P) and stop bars on both SR 1304 approaches.
- Added All Way plaques (R1-3P) to existing Stop signs (R1-1) and installed supplemental Stop signs (R1-1) with All Way plaques (R1-3P) to have dual-indicated Stop signs as well as stop bars on both SR 1308 approaches.
- Installed two sets of transverse rumble strips (wider spacing in first set, narrower spacing in 2nd set) and a supplemental Stop Ahead warning sign (W3-1) to have dual-indicated Stop Ahead warning signs in advance of intersection on both SR 1308 approaches.
- Installed dual-indicated Stop Ahead warning signs (W3-1) and two sets of transverse rumble strips (wider spacing in first set, narrower spacing in 2nd set) in advance of intersection on both SR 1304 approaches.

- Construction period extended approximately two months beyond the project completion date to account for any temporary warning signs or other modifications implemented after the conversion to AWSC.
- The A-injury TC in the before period was an angle crash on Sunday, September 27, 2020 at 9:15 AM involving an EB vehicle on SR 1308 that ran the stop sign at 45 mph and struck an SB vehicle on SR 1304 at 50 mph under daylight, dry conditions.
- All 3 EB at-fault TCs involved striking SB vehicles on SR 1304, while 2 of the 3 WB at-fault TCs involved striking NB vehicles on SR 1304 and the remaining WB TC involved striking an SB vehicle.
- Only 1 of the 7 before period crashes occurred under dark conditions; the remaining 6, including all 3 B-injury crashes and the A-injury crash, occurred under daylight conditions.
- The 1 non-TC in the before period was a sideswipe same-direction crash between NB vehicles involving improper passing in the intersection (March 2019, C-injury).
- No crashes occurred during the 4-year after period, representing a 100% reduction in total crashes, target crashes, and severity.
- The west leg of SR 1308 was resurfaced between 11/2021 and 4/2023, and as of 11/2023, the transverse rumble strips on EB SR 1308 had not been reinstalled following the resurfacing.

- This intersection was on the NCDOT HSIP list from 2017 to 2023, and the AWSC improvement was a recommendation from the 2019 study. 
- There was a significant road closure on SR 1214 from 7/10/2025 to 12/17/2025, due to a bridge replacement project. There did not appear to be any significant crash pattern within this time period, as there was 1 crash (Angle, WB at fault, 12/16/2025) that occurred within this window. This crash was also the last recorded incident in the After Period.
- Of the 10 Before Period Target Crashes, 8 of them involved an eastbound vehicle on SR 1214 being struck, and 2 involved a westbound vehicle. 
- In the After Period, both of the crashes in which the at-fault vehicle ran the posted STOP sign involved eastbound or westbound vehicles on SR 1214 being at fault (1 of each), while both of the Failure to Yield crashes involved a southbound vehicle on SR 1222 being at fault.
- The 3 non-Target Crashes in the Before Period included a sideswipe, opposite direction crash on SR 1214, a rear-end crash on eastbound SR 1214, and a RTDR crash involving a vehicle pulling out of the restaurant PVA along the south leg of SR 1222.
Treatment data includes all crashes at the intersection of SR 1214 (Boykin Bridge Road/Elizabeth Street) at SR 1222 (Beulah Road), with a Y-line of 150 feet

- Construction period extended approximately two months beyond the project completion date to account for any temporary warning signs or other modifications implemented after the conversion to AWSC.
- The A-injury TC in the before period (May 2017) involved a SB vehicle on SR 1758 that ran the stop sign at approximately 50 mph, striking an EB vehicle on SR 1006.
- The B-injury TC (January 2020) involved a NB vehicle on SR 1758 failing to yield for a WB vehicle on SR 1006 traveling at 55 mph.
- The 1 non-TC in the before period that resulted in a fatality involved an impaired driver losing control after spinning their tires in the intersection and running off the road at 1:34 AM (March 2018).
- All 12 TCs across both periods occurred during daylight, dry conditions.
- Both EB SR 1006 at-fault TCs in the after period occurred within the first two months following the AWSC conversion (October and November 2021).
- The 2 no-fault TCs in the after period involved unusual circumstances: one where both vehicles failed to yield with no fault determined (March 2024, C-injury), and one where a construction worker instructed both vehicles to proceed simultaneously (September 2025, PDO). The construction being completed could not be determined.
- The 1 non-TC in the after period involved a SB garbage truck on SR 1758 that snagged overhead cable lines with a raised bed (January 2024, PDO).
- After an initial cluster of 3 TCs in the first 6 months following the AWSC conversion, only 2 TCs occurred over the remaining 3 years and 10 months of the after period, and both involved unusual no-fault circumstances rather than the failure-to-yield/ran-stop-sign pattern that dominated the before period.

- This study location was contained within a larger evaluation's limits (04-15-35863), which included all of SR 1003 (Buffalo Road) from SR 1702 (Archer Lodge Road) to the Wake County line. The improvements of the larger section included shoulder widening and ditch piping along SR 1003, but since the dates of these improvements and those of this evaluation were significantly aligned, the section included in this evaluation was omitted from Evaluation 04-15-35863. 
- Dark condition crashes made up 10 of 24 (41.7%) of Target Crashes and 18 of 42 (42.9%) of total crashes in the Before Period, and 1 of 2 (50%) of Target Crashes and 14 of 17 (82.4%) of total crashes in the After Period. 
- A pattern of run through intersection crashes, in which a vehicle runs straight through the STOP sign on the minor approach and off the road on the opposite side of the intersection is present in the both the Before and After Periods, with there being 5 such crashes at the SR 1716 intersection and 1 at the SR 2638 intersection in the Before Period, and 6 such crashes at the SR 2638 intersection and 1 at the SR 1716 intersection in the After Period. 
- There were 13 total crashes in the Construction Period, including 7 (53.8%) Target Crashes, all 7 occurring at the SR 2638 intersection. 
- The significant increase in severity index for Target #2 crashes can be attributed to the fact that the only Target #2 crash in the After Period was a C-injury crash, while 2 of the 3 Before Period Target #2 crashes were Property Damage Only, lowering the overall severity.

• Construction period set with the project completion date of May 24, 2021 near the middle to account for any temporary warning signs or other modifications implemented before or after the conversion to AWSC. No crashes occurred at the intersection during the construction period.
• All Target Crashes in both periods were angle crashes.
• The Class A injury Target Crash was a 12/16/2017 angle crash at 11:43 AM in which an EB vehicle on SR 1617 ran the stop sign at 55 mph and struck the saddle fuel tank of a SB tractor/semi-trailer on SR 1001; the truck ran off the road and came to rest in the front yard of a residence.
• The most severe after-period Target Crash was a 10/23/2025 angle crash at 12:53 PM in which a WB vehicle on SR 1001 ran the stop sign and struck a NB vehicle towing a trailer on SR 1617, resulting in one Class C injury.
• A breakdown by the at-fault direction of the Target Crashes is as follows:
   - Before: EB SR 1617: 8 (6 failure-to-yield, 2 ran-stop-sign); WB SR 1619: 4 (3 failure-to-yield, 1 ran-stop-sign)
   - After: NB SR 1001: 3 (2 failure-to-yield, 1 ran-stop-sign); WB SR 1001: 1 (ran-stop-sign); EB SR 1617: 1 (failure-to-yield); no fault could be determined: 2
• The after-period Target Crashes where fault could not be determined both involved a SB vehicle on SR 1001 and a vehicle on the cross street (1 EB SR 1617 and 1 WB SR 1619) colliding in the intersection. Coded speeds in both crashes were 15 mph or less, consistent with vehicles entering from their stops rather than running them.
• The one non-Target Crash in the after period involved a SB vehicle on SR 1001 that failed to reduce speed and struck a vehicle stopped at the all-way stop (December 2024, Class C). Rear-end frequency did not change with the conversion: one in each period, both queue crashes.
